contract.title: ontoTF: researcher-first XML mappings
contract.purpose: Help a researcher find justified correspondences between native Text-Fabric or Context-Fabric annotations and entities in other corpora, with an explicit distinction between category mappings and entity identity.
contract.authority: This document supersedes ADR-001's planned data registries, per-batch release protocols and attestation workflow. It is a target contract, not a claim that current Python code already reads XML. Historical releases remain historical; new development must not expand their authoring machinery.

requirements.requirement: The sole editable source of active mappings for corpus X is src/tfont/mappings/X.xml. A contributor edits that file, or creates it for a new corpus. No manifest, Python switch, import list, version registry, review packet, generated JSON, code file or workflow needs editing. A second file is optional only for genuinely separate evidence supplied voluntarily by the contributor, never as part of the publication protocol.

All new authoritative mapping records and their optional annotations are checked into this repository as XML. Historical JSON artifacts may remain temporarily for compatibility but never become another source of truth. Do not introduce a database, hosted mapping service, YAML/JSON ledger, triplestore or generated committed mapping mirror.

Native corpus annotations remain authoritative. Exact, close, broader, narrower, related, ambiguous, native-only and unsupported are distinct. "Broader" means the native meaning is broader than the target; "narrower" means the native meaning is narrower than the target. Approximate links are opt-in and never silently promoted to exact equivalence.

A shared ontology class maps native annotation categories, not individual token identities. An entity-level mapping needs a native identifier and a common external entity IRI. No corpus-to-corpus individual equivalence may be inferred only from a shared class or matching gloss.

Store the source corpus name in the XML root and, where known, its release or source revision. An optional evidence URI and note on a mapping may point to definitions. Reviewers verify scholarly assertions against actual source definitions. No signatures, checksums, attestations, certificate chains, lock registries or per-row review receipts.

The Python package discovers corpus XML files by filename, not hardcoded corpus enumerations. Each file is independently loaded: adding a corpus requires no edits to central Python, release catalogs or other XML files. Packaged wheels contain the same XML mapping data as the source tree.

Read XML with Python's standard library, construct in-memory native-to-target and target-to-native indexes from the same records, and execute selectors using already-loaded TF/Context-Fabric APIs. No RDF conversion, ontology HTTP fetch or external service is required to answer a query. Do not create intermediate release files in the repository.

One PR may contain any coherent number of mapping decisions. One logically independent, counterexample-seeking adversarial review pass is required before merge and may be performed by the authoring agent in a separate pass. Review the semantic claims and negative examples. Git's diff and normal PR discussion are the audit trail. No separate reviewer identity, challenge-response protocol or cryptographic approval.

For mapping-only changes use one CI workflow that parses XML, validates basic syntax and selector requirements, detects conflicting duplicates, tests representative forward and reverse lookups, and builds a wheel. No per-corpus/per-feature workflows, research tickets, design PRs, frozen coverage manifests or profile releases. New runtime behavior requires appropriate TDD and review in the same PR.

Support additional corpora and ontology IRIs as data, not as hardcoded switches. Retain essential native provenance and licensing notices. Prefer a missing/uncertain result over a fabricated correspondence. No arbitrary quota of rows, ontology families or mandatory coverage denominator gates.

xml-format.root: <mappings corpus="..." source="..." corpusVersion="..."> Optional corpusVersion identifies the actual native source release. It is not an ontoTF profile version. An individual map may override corpusVersion when the source interpretation differs between releases.
xml-format.record: Each <map> has kind and relation. A positive relation needs an absolute target IRI; ambiguous/native-only/unsupported have no target. 'node' maps an annotation node type; 'feature' maps a native feature; 'value' maps a feature/value selector on a node type; 'edge' maps a TF edge feature, optionally restricted by from/to node types; and 'entity' resolves an individual through a native node type plus a feature/value identifier and maps to an external identity IRI. For entity mappings, the selector must uniquely resolve the individual before an exact identity claim is returned.
xml-format.validation: No per-row UUID or digest. The validator checks filename equals corpus, one-to-one required selector fields for each kind, relation/target consistency, absolute target IRI, repeated identical rows and contradictory exact assertions to clearly incompatible targets. It does not pronounce an ontology claim true because a URL or checksum is well formed.

example.description: Two corpus category mappings and one conservative disposition

query-contract.operation: List discovered XML corpora; do not require a registry.
Return target IRIs, relation and optional evidence for one native selector.

Given source corpus, native selector and destination corpus, match through a common target IRI. Exact mappings produce exact CATEGORY correspondences, not individual token alignments. Entity identity requires entity mappings. Approximate paths are returned only when explicitly requested and keep relation and direction. If no justified mapping exists, return an empty result with an intelligible diagnostic.

When a target corpus TF dataset is already loaded and its selector is supported, execute the native query to return matching nodes. Otherwise return a mapping recommendation rather than inventing node matches.

acceptance.check: Adding five or fifty mappings to an existing corpus changes exactly one authored XML file, with no generated files committed.
Adding a new corpus requires one XML file and zero Python/CI/registry edits.
Both directions of BHSA Noun and Syriac Noun lookup work from installed wheel XML.
The runtime never infers that two noun tokens are the same individual merely because both map to OLiA Noun.
Approximate/non-target rows never masquerade as exact counterparts.
Invalid XML and structurally invalid native selectors fail with the source file and mapping location; one bad corpus does not hide healthy corpora.
Every substantive mapping PR receives an evidence-first adversarial review once; ordinary PRs use one nonduplicated CI workflow.

non-requirements.item: Cryptographic provenance, signed review receipts, protected handoffs and GitHub identity attestation.
Immutable copy-forward profiles, semantic release versions per batch or profile-specific package builds.
Mandatory research-plan-TDD paperwork for another value of an already supported selector type.
Download all seven ontologies, pre-enumerate all features or reach a fixed coverage target before usable search works.
Run a separate CI job or workflow for every corpus, feature, ontology or historical issue.
Convert TF corpora to RDF or distribute upstream corpus data.
